newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - focus on new issue market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - focus on new issue market.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat at midday as players turned their attention to a heavy new issue calendar.
"The focus is all on the primary market and none on the secondary," one trader said.
New issues are expected to total $1.3 billion for Wednesday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
The Lower Colorado River Authority, Texas, topped off the busy new issue calendar with a $205 million competitive issue won by Merrill Lynch & Co.
Merrill reoffered the 2012 maturity at a 5.30 percent yield.

In negotiated action, Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authoriyt, N.Y., sold $200 million revenue bonds through senior manager PaineWebber Inc. The firm tentatively priced the offering to yield 5.65 percent in 2027.
Bear Stearns & Co said it tentatively priced $140.8 million Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development revenue bonds at a top yield 5.95 percent in 2028.
One trader said pricing was "very aggresive" on the new deals, especially the Maryland issue. "If these levels are anywhere near correct, then the market's hot," the trader said.
In the muni secondary, bids on Chicago Skyway 5-1/2s of 2023 were up two basis points to 5.78 percent net. Texas Turnpike Authority 5-1/4s of 2023 were one basis point higher, at 5.60 percent net.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 3/32 at 117-7/32, while December T-bonds were 1/32 lower at 115-6/32. The MOB spread was 65 ticks, compared to 61 ticks at the close Tuesday.
In follow-through action from Tuesday, Smith Barney Inc said it had a $17.5 million balance remaining on San Francisco International Airport's $118.5 million revenue bond deal.
